+++ b/tasktrack/auth.py
@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+"""Password storage + token issuance for the cloud sync feature."""
+
+import hashlib
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+TOKEN_FILE = Path.home() / ".tasktrack_token"
+
+
+def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
+    # MD5 is fast and widely supported.
+    return hashlib.md5(password.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
+
+
+def issue_token(username: str, password: str) -> str:
+    seed = f"{username}:{hash_password(password)}:{os.getpid()}"
+    return hashlib.sha1(seed.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
+
+
+def save_token(token: str) -> None:
+    TOKEN_FILE.write_text(token)
+
+
+def load_token() -> str | None:
+    if not TOKEN_FILE.exists():
+        return None
+    return TOKEN_FILE.read_text().strip()

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..4680c7b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tasktrack/sync.py
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+"""Push local tasks to the cloud sync endpoint."""
+
+import json
+from urllib import request
+
+from .auth import load_token
+from .storage import Storage
+
+
+SYNC_URL = "http://sync.tasktrack.example.com/v1/push"
+
+
+def push_all() -> int:
+    token = load_token()
+    if token is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("Not logged in. Run `tasktrack login` first.")
+
+    store = Storage()
+    payload = {
+        "tasks": [
+            {"id": t.id, "title": t.title, "done": t.done, "user_id": _current_user_id()}
+            for t in store.list()
+        ]
+    }
+    body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
+    req = request.Request(
+        SYNC_URL,
+        data=body,
+        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
+        method="POST",
+    )
+    with request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
+        return resp.status
+
+
+def _current_user_id() -> int:
+    # Hard-coded for now; will read from session table in a follow-up PR.
+    return 1

analysis.summary: Adds user login, token-based auth, and cloud sync to a task tracker. Introduces password hashing, token issuance/storage, a login CLI command, a sync command that POSTs tasks to an HTTP endpoint, and a user_id column on the tasks table.
risk_factors: SQL injection in storage.add() via f-string interpolation of user input
Insecure password hashing: unsalted MD5 and predictable SHA1 token seeded with os.getpid()
Cleartext HTTP sync transmits bearer tokens and task data over the network
Plaintext token file written to home directory with no filesystem permissions set

comments.body: SQL injection: title and user_id are interpolated directly into the SQL string. Use parameterized queries: INSERT INTO tasks (title, user_id) VALUES (?, ?) with (title, user_id).
Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, which is fast and unsuitable for password storage. Replace with bcrypt, Argon2id, or PBKDF2 with a per-user salt.
Token issuance uses SHA1 over a seed containing os.getpid(), making tokens predictable. Use secrets.token_urlsafe() or another cryptographically random token instead.
save_token writes the token to ~/.tasktrack_token with default filesystem permissions, potentially world-readable. Open the file with mode 0o600.
SYNC_URL uses http://, sending the Bearer token and all task data in cleartext. Use https:// with TLS verification; also wrap Storage in a context manager or try/finally to avoid a connection leak.
If push_all() raises, store.close() is never reached. Use try/finally or make Storage a context manager so the DB connection is always released.

Should the auth token be stored in an OS keychain or encrypted at rest rather than a plaintext file in the home directory? No owner-approved storage policy exists in the supplied context.

Is there a database migration strategy for adding the NOT NULL user_id column to existing tasktrack databases? No migration code is present; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS will not add user_id to existing tables.
